notes:
High-level: Aurora SupportOps runs a multi-tenant contact-center SaaS for EU retailers and telcos. They need dedicated throughput for 24/7 agent-assist across regions plus guaranteed burst headroom for marketing campaigns. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private control plane for strongest isolation and EU data residency.

Primary contacts and asks:
- Eva Kova07 (Head of Support Platforms) - buyer; must have predictable p95 latency during campaign spikes and clear rollback paths.
- Marcus Berg (CTO) - wants VPC-only control plane, HSM/KMS integration, and proof that no model state is leaked between tenants.
- Anya Varela (Ops) - will run traffic replay for acceptance; cares about monitoring and token-cost visibility.

Technical requirements (from 2026-02-20 kick-off):
- Workloads: real-time agent assist (multi-turn), post-call ticket summarization (batch), automated tool-calling (secure signed actions to backend), conversational search over recent tickets.
- Latency targets: p95 assistant response <= 250-350ms depending on payload (short prompts); streaming perceived latency < 120ms for interactive typing.
- Throughput: steady-state ~450 concurrent agents across EU region, peak bursts to ~1,500 concurrent during promos (10-15x short spikes).
- SLA: 99.95% availability; require documented fallback model variant and automatic routing policy for degraded capacity.
- Multi-tenancy: strict isolation per customer; logs partitioned, KMS per-tenant preferred for keys.
- Data residency: EU-only for core tenants; allowed staging in na for non-sensitive workloads.

POC and acceptance plan:
- 3-week POC using dedicated pool sizing: Week 1 baseline ingest + smoke tests, Week 2 replay Black Friday peak, Week 3 soak & canary rollback tests.
- Acceptance: maintain p95 under 350ms at 2x replay load; SCIM + SSO tested; audit logs retained and exportable; no cross-tenant traces in logs.

Quotes from calls: "We need hard guarantees around latency and a transparent cost model for burst capacity. If costs blow out it will be a non-starter." 026-02-20 Eva.

Operational notes: 
- Preference for reserved GPUs with burst autoscale configured as guaranteed headroom but within committed spend.
- Wants Redwood Optimize to provide batching/caching suggestions tailored to multi-tenant conversational patterns to lower token spend.
- Required integrations: SCIM for provisioning, SAML SSO, KMS/HSM for encryption, and Syslog export for audit ingest.

Risk areas: 
- Legal/DPA delays (EU residency clauses).
- Network peering windows may push POC timing into April maintenance window.
- Procurement wants 12-month committed pricing and SLAs before sign-off.

Internal AE notes: 
- Competitive win if we demonstrate 25% unit cost savings and stable p95 under synthetic 3x traffic.
- Recommend offering trial pricing for POC and discounted reserved capacity if committed ARR met.
